Metadata in documents and presentations made with Claude — and how to remove it

When Claude creates a Word document, a PowerPoint presentation, a spreadsheet or a PDF, it writes the file with open-source code libraries. Those libraries fill in the document properties with their own names and default dates. Here is what to look for and how to clean it.

Updated 2026-11-22 · 5 min read
Short answer: Files Claude creates don’t say “Claude”, but the libraries used to generate them leave their own traces: names such as python-docx, python-pptx, PptxGenJS or ReportLab, dates from 2013 and authors like “Steve Canny”. IA Cleaner removes them without changing your content.

Why these files have unusual metadata

Claude doesn’t open Word or PowerPoint. It runs code that builds the file, typically with libraries such as python-docx, python-pptx, openpyxl, ReportLab, docx (JavaScript) or PptxGenJS. Each library leaves its own defaults in the document properties. We generated files with each of them and found these values:

  • python-docx (Word): Author python-docx, created and modified on 23 December 2013, application Microsoft Macintosh Word.
  • python-pptx (PowerPoint): description generated using python-pptx, last modified by Steve Canny (the library’s author) and dates from January 2013.
  • openpyxl (Excel): Author openpyxl and application Microsoft Excel Compatible / Openpyxl.
  • ReportLab (PDF): producer ReportLab PDF Library, author anonymous, title untitled.
  • docx for JavaScript (Word): author and last modified by Un-named.
  • PptxGenJS (PowerPoint): title and subject PptxGenJS Presentation, author and company PptxGenJS.

None of these says “Claude”, but anyone who opens File → Properties sees a document that wasn’t made in Office, often with a date years in the past. The same applies to files created by other AI assistants that write code.

Remove it with IA Cleaner

  1. Download the file from Claude.
  2. Open IA Cleaner → Documents and drop the .docx, .pptx, .xlsx or PDF.
  3. The report lists every property found (author, last modified by, description, application, company, dates).
  4. Click Download clean document. Your text, slides and layout don’t change.

We tested the six kinds of file above: after cleaning, none of those values remains anywhere in the file. Nothing is uploaded.

Opening and re-saving in Office isn’t enough

If you open the file in Word or PowerPoint and save it, Office updates some fields (for example “last modified by”), but the original author, creation date and description usually stay. Clean the file, then add your own details if you want them.

And the text you copy from Claude?

Text copied from a chat can bring invisible characters or special spaces. Paste it in IA Cleaner → Text to see and remove them. Metadata cleaning doesn’t change your writing, so it isn’t about AI detectors that judge style.

Who is “Steve Canny”?

He is the author of the python-pptx library. His name is saved as “last modified by” in presentations generated with the library’s default template, so it shows up in files he had nothing to do with. Seeing it is a sign the file was generated by code.

Files from ChatGPT and other assistants

ChatGPT and other assistants that create files by running code usually rely on the same Python libraries, so their Word, PowerPoint, Excel and PDF files can carry the same traces. The cleaning works the same way. For the wider picture, see AI traces in documents and emails.

What IA Cleaner detects and removes

In PDF, Word, Excel and PowerPoint files it identifies and removes author, company, last editor, generating app, template, editing time, XMP and the metadata of embedded images. Your content stays the same. You see the full report first — every block found, with AI-related ones flagged — and then download the clean copy.
